title: Vittorio De Sica's birth chart
metaDescription: Vittorio De Sica's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.6° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, mutable leads with five. Mutable weight is read as flexibility, and the old texts are frank that its cost is scatter.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 14.6° Cancer. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the classical scheme — a water sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Cancer (24.0°), Venus in Leo (2.7°), Mars in Virgo (26.4°): a mind that absorbs before it argues, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun opposition Saturn, 1.6° of separation. Oppositions are read as full-moon geometry — maximum visibility between two needs that share one spine. Behind it, Mercury sextile Mars at 2.4°, and Mars square Neptune at 3.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Jupiter in Capricorn at 7.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Capricorn at 13.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 3, earth 3, fire 2, air 2 across the elements, and mutable 5, cardinal 4, fixed 1 across the modalities. Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 22.7°.
